text:
Sam Carter: Hey — quick question on SDK telemetry behavior. I added a quiet mode for a customer (they set clientMetrics=false) and saw that our SDK still sends `X-User-Agent` and trace headers on retry/fallback requests. Is that expected or a bug?

Jess Li: Short answer: we tried to keep UA for routing/compat but should respect opt-outs for telemetry metrics. Need to check which headers we consider "operational" vs "telemetry". @sam can you paste the headers you observed?

Sam Carter: Sure, from a single streaming session reconnect log: 
```
> POST /v1/stream
> X-User-Agent: RedwoodSDK/1.4.0 node/18
> X-Client-Metrics: 0
> traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
```
I expected no metrics headers and minimal UA, but traceparent is the one I'm worried about (PII/privacy concerns).

Mike Huang: We intentionally preserve `traceparent` for request correlation through retries so errors and fallbacks are linkable in logs/traces. But we should not send tokenized metrics payloads if clientMetrics=false. Reconnects: if the streaming connection is re-established for the same logical request we currently reuse the same trace id. If a full fallback (different model/region) is triggered we create a new trace.

Olivia Park: From a compliance POV customers asked to disable any identifier that could persist across calls. `traceparent` is short-lived but still an identifier. Do we have a knob to completely disable trace propagation?

Jess Li: We do have `tracing.enabled` in the SDK config, but it's opt-in by default. The bug here is that quiet/disable-metrics toggles didn't cascade to tracing in some streaming reconnect code paths. Proposed patch: treat `clientMetrics=false` as not implying `tracing.enabled=false` (explicit), but add a top-level `privacyMode: true` that disables both UA and trace propagation. Example config: 
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  clientMetrics: false,        // keeps perf counters off
  tracing: { enabled: false },
  privacyMode: true           // full opt-out: UA + traceparent suppressed
});
```
We'd then: (1) strip `X-User-Agent`, (2) remove `traceparent`/`tracestate`, (3) ensure reconnects do not restore traces when privacyMode=true.

Sam Carter: That sounds reasonable. One more edge: streaming reconnects that happen inside the same TCP session but after auth refresh — we observed the SDK re-inserts `X-User-Agent` during auth refresh flow. Example log snippet: 
```
[stream] reconnecting after 401, sending auth refresh
headers: { Authorization: "Bearer <masked>", X-User-Agent: "RedwoodSDK/1.4.0" }
```
Would privacyMode suppress that too?

Mike Huang: Yes, privacyMode should be enforced at the request builder layer (before auth) so even during refresh we don't add those headers. I'll add a unit that simulates auth-refresh+reconnect and assert headers absent.

ci-bot: link to proposed PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/ (add tests + changelog note) :white_check_mark:

Jess Li: I'll draft the PR — will include: tests for streaming reconnect, auth refresh path, and a small doc blurb about privacyMode. Also will add server-side handling note: if a client strips traces we still accept and create server traces but don't link back to client ids.

Sam Carter: Awesome — thanks. @jess assign me for the streaming test harness and @mike for the reconnect logic review. :thumbsup:
